issues.legal_issue: A decree for eviction cannot be entered on admission of the landlord-tenant relationship alone when the tenant raises a disputed defence that goes to the root of the claim.
material_facts: In the eviction suit, the tenant admitted the landlord-tenant relationship and the lease period.
The tenant claimed that the parties had entered into an agreement for sale of the premises and that he had paid a substantial advance under it; the landlord denied that claim.
The tenant had also brought a contested suit for specific performance based on the alleged agreement.
The trial court granted eviction under Order XII Rule 6 CPC, and the Supreme Court found that the disputed issues required the tenant to have an opportunity to contest the suit.
issues.conclusion: The admission of the tenancy relationship was not an unequivocal admission entitling the landlord to an eviction decree under Order XII Rule 6 CPC. The matter was remitted for fresh consideration, subject to the tenant paying the arrears and ongoing compensation specified by the Court; the Court expressed no opinion on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Order XII Rule 6 CPC is an enabling and discretionary provision: judgment on admission is not a matter of right, and where a defendant raises objections going to the root of the case, the court should not exercise that discretion merely on the basis of an admission that does not unequivocally establish entitlement to the decree. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: eviction_suit_with_judgment_on_admissions_application and tenancy_relationship_admitted and material_defence_raised and landlord_disputes_material_defence

predicates.eviction_suit_with_judgment_on_admission: A plaintiff seeks eviction and asks the court to decide the claim on admissions.
predicates.tenancy_relationship_admitted: The tenant admits that the landlord-tenant relationship exists.
predicates.material_defence_raised: The tenant raises a defence that, if established, could affect the right to eviction.
predicates.landlord_disputes_material_defence: The landlord contests the tenant’s material defence.

issues.definition: When an eviction claim is presented for decision on admissions, the tenancy relationship is admitted, and a material defence is raised and disputed, the claim requires a fresh hearing.
